newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGIP says portfolio balancing behind Valeo move.
newsitem.headline: CGIP says portfolio balancing behind Valeo move.

text.p: French holding company CGIP reduced its stake in Crown Cork and Seal to add to its Valeo stake as part of a strategic rebalancing of its investment portfolio, CGIP's chairman said on Tuesday.

Ernest-Antoine Seilliere told a news conference that the reduction of the Crown Cork stake last month to 9.9 percent from 20 percent, and the purchase of a 20 percent stake in Valeo announced earlier on Tuesday, were "parallel operations".
CGIP had held around 49 percent of its assets in the packaging business as a result of its holding in Crown Cork, acquired last year in exchange for a stake in Carnaud Metalbox last year, he said.

Packaging now makes up 21 percent of CGIP's strategic interests, he said. Other leading categories of investment are automobile equipment at 25 percent (through Valeo), information technology services at 21 percent (through Cap Gemini ) and non-quoted assets at 33 percent, Seilliere said.

He said international investors had told CGIP that packaging was a mature business and that if investors wanted to buy into the packaging industry they would buy Crown Cork shares directly. But if they wanted to avoid the sector they would not buy CGIP shares.
To rebalance the portfolio, CGIP has cut its stake in Crown Cork and boosted its holding in Valeo which has significant growth potential, Seilliere said.
Valeo has a sales target of 40 billion francs by 2000 compared to sales of 25 billion francs in 1995, he said.

Valeo was attractive to CGIP as CGIP had entered Valeo's capital 10 years ago and knew the company, he said. Valeo aimed to be a leader in a world market experiencing growth and had a balance sheet that allowed financing for acquisitions.
Valeo also has a high level of investment in research and development, Seilliere said.

Earlier on Tuesday, CGIP said it was buying 20 percent of Valeo in a deal valuing the car parts manufacturer at 330 francs per share. Italian-controlled holding company Cerus, which sold the stake to CGIP, said it had also sold stakes of 3.6 percent each to French state bank CDC and JP Morgan.
